issues.finding: When A is empty, the choice function for nonempty subsets is undefined at A, so the displayed initial value does not apply.
issues.proposed_resolution: Handle the empty set as already well-ordered, then run the recursion only for nonempty A.

issues.location: stop-marker convention and subsequent injectivity and range claims
issues.finding: The source says to set g(delta)=A for all delta<=alpha when stopping at alpha, overwriting previous chosen values. A constant tail is not injective and has a marker outside A, so later injectivity, range and bijection statements need the pre-stop restriction. After the marker is inserted, the displayed equality test A=image(g|alpha) would become false again and incorrectly call f on an empty remainder.
issues.proposed_resolution: Set the marker for delta>=alpha, make the stopping test A subseteq image(g|alpha) persistent after the marker, prove injectivity before the first stop, and use the initial-segment restriction for the range and final bijection.

issues.location: Hartogs contradiction if the recursive choice process never stops
issues.finding: The source claims strict cardinal inequality from every ordinal into Pow(A) minus empty, though g takes values in A and supplies only an injection from each ordinal into A. Hartogs' lemma applies directly to A.
issues.proposed_resolution: Use cardle(alpha,A) for every ordinal alpha in the no-stop supposition, contradicting Hartogs' lemma for A.

translation_treatment: The target handles the empty input, makes the stop marker and condition persistent, restricts the bijection to pre-stop values, and applies Hartogs to A. Potter's page citation is localized. The frozen source remains unchanged.
